_ruling: A test was written to match the code. I do not care AT ALL about code coverage. The ONLY thing tests should be validating is the requirements. If we are making up tests for coverage that do not map onto requirements then either (a) we are wasting time, or (b) we have identified a new acceptance criteria and we need to retro as to why it wasn't discovered earlier. (human, 2026-08-02)
_why_this_file_exists: DEF-ROC-045. Until this file landed, `make test-requirement-gate PROJECT=ROC` returned TRG-VERDICT: NOT-CONFIGURED with files=0 cases=0, and loop-gate check 6 printed that verdict every single cycle for weeks. Two agents hit it independently. The tool was explicit that NOT-CONFIGURED is not clean, so this was never a silent tool failure -- it was a silent COVERAGE gap: the one project whose defects were all being found by hand had no gate looking at its tests at all. §17i: a control that cannot report is not a control, and silence is never a pass.
_mode_why: RATCHET, not enforce. The honest first measurement (2026-08-24, DEF-ROC-045) is 1144 untagged cases of 3210 scanned and 3 authored preconditions. Enforcing on day one would turn every ROC pull red for debt nobody has triaged, and a gate that is red for everything is a gate everyone learns to ignore -- which is exactly how `make render-diagrams` sat red on trunk for 20 days in this same project. So the committed baseline is the FLOOR and it may ONLY SHRINK: a NEW violation blocks the loop, the existing debt is reported every run until the retro decides, per the ruling, whether each case is waste or an undiscovered acceptance criterion. Clearing the floor by mass-tagging is a FAILED experiment (EXP-124), not progress.
_fileHeaderCoversCounts_why: A file-level `@covers` is a coverage claim about the MODULE; the ruling asks what THIS CASE validates. Kept strict, matching OagEventSource. The number it costs is reported separately as `acCoveredByFileHeaderOnly` (326 of the 1144) so a retro can see the price of the strictness and change this flag if it disagrees.

roots.why: The whole ROC test corpus: the Function App (tests/unit, tests/acceptance, tests/live), the dashboard (component, domain, api and Playwright e2e specs) and the replay-injector tool. Both limbs apply. `src/infra` holds no test files today; it is inside this root so any Terraform-side test lands under the gate automatically rather than needing a config change nobody remembers to make.

Cross-project agent-ops tooling that ROC agents edit (loop-gate, impacted-tests, isolated-commit, this gate). Scanned deliberately so a violation added from an ROC session blocks the ROC loop rather than only surfacing whenever another project's loop next runs. The limb-1 exemption for machinery invariant tests is taken as a VISIBLE allowlist entry below, not by silently omitting the limb here.

The work-item machinery (python). Limb 1 does not apply: limb-1 case parsing is JS/TS only, and these are machinery invariant tests with no product acceptance criterion. Limb 2's exec-boundary rule DOES apply and it currently finds one real hit here.

corpus._readerModules_why: `real-peek-rows` is ROC's own real-capture module: the replay-injector's REAL_PEEK_MATRIX is three verbatim rows peeked off the live PPSM Service Bus. Without it named here, limb 2 could not see a mutation of the only multi-file real capture ROC has, and the gate would have reported clean over it -- the exact blindness DEF-ROC-045 is about.
corpus._fixturePathTokens_why: MEASURED, not copied. ROC's idiom is `resolve(here, "fixtures", name)` -- the path segment is a SEPARATE argument, so the default `fixtures/` token (with the slash) matches none of it. Shipping the default list would have left limb 2 at 0 across the whole app test tree while looking configured, so the quoted bare-word forms and the `LIVE_CAPTURE` constant (def075's real wire capture) are named explicitly.

derived._why: `FoldedAlertState` is ROC's one fold-derived aggregate: every field here is derived by folding the decision log for one alert identity, so hand-setting one builds a prior no real decision stream can hold. `heldUntil` matters most -- the fold copies it VERBATIM off the terminal record and never re-derives it (delta 019 A8) precisely so a fixture edit cannot silently re-date a live hold; a test that hand-sets it re-introduces by hand the thing that invariant exists to prevent. FINDS ZERO TODAY, stated rather than left as a comfortable silence: no ROC test currently uses the `{...} as FoldedAlertState` cast form the rule matches, and the rule cannot see a folded field hand-set through a LOCAL BUILDER (a documented recall gap of the tool, not of this config). It is declared now so the first hand-set fold prior is caught at the moment it is written.

allowlist.why: Agent-system MACHINERY invariant tests. They assert a tool's own contract (impacted-tests' node->spec lookup, this gate's own rules) and there is no product acceptance criterion for them to name -- the requirement they serve is a PROCESS obligation, not a customer one. Limb 2 still applies to them in full. Same entry, same reason, as the OagEventSource config.

A MEASURED FALSE POSITIVE, allowlisted visibly rather than by weakening the corpus config for everyone. The three hits spread an override over `deps(...)` -- a PORT-FAKE DEPENDENCY BUNDLE (allowlist, resolveAuth, createSender, logger), not a captured record. It is tainted only by cascade: the file-scoped taint set has no lexical scoping, so `const parseRows = vi.fn(realRows)` taints the identifier `parseRows`, which is also a PARAMETER NAME in the `deps` factory, which taints `deps`. Substituting an adapter on a deps bundle is the correct hexagonal test idiom and authors no precondition about reality. Scoped to this one file and this one rule so a genuine mutation of REAL_PEEK_MATRIX anywhere in the replay-injector -- including in this file, under the delete/mutate rules -- still fires.

_baseline_why: MEASURED 2026-08-24 at the first configured run (DEF-ROC-045), honestly and without mass-tagging. 342 files, 3210 cases scanned. LIMB 1 = 1144 cases (36%) with no AC reference in their own title, their suite, or their comments; 326 of the 1144 carry a file-level @covers and nothing per-case. Where it sits: 809 in work/ROC/src/app/tests, 223 in the dashboard's colocated component/domain/api specs, 96 in the dashboard Playwright e2e specs, 16 in the replay-injector. Nothing in .claude/tools after the machinery allowlist. Worth the retro's attention: ROC already writes AC tags heavily (3674 occurrences, in BOTH the `AC-076-2` hyphen family and the `AC-030.2` dot family), so this is not a project that never adopted the vocabulary -- it is a project where roughly a third of cases were written without naming what they validate, and the dashboard's colocated specs are the densest pocket. LIMB 2 = 3 static hits, each read individually at the first run: (1) .claude/skills/work-items/scripts/test_work_items.py:2912 exec-boundary-stubbed -- shared machinery debt, also carried in the OagEventSource baseline, so a fix slacks both ratchets at once; (2)+(3) def075NotHandledProbe.test.ts:105/106 delete-on-real-capture and mutate-real-capture, where `withReason()` deletes and re-sets `noAlertReason` on a copy of the REAL captured record. Those two are TRUE POSITIVES in shape but the test already DECLARES the synthetic in words -- 'Reality has not produced one yet -- the field ships in this commit -- so this confirms nothing about the wire (v123 rule 4)' -- which is the remedy the ruling accepts. They are left in the BASELINE rather than allowlisted on purpose: per the ruling the gate never makes the choice, so the retro decides whether a declared synthetic earns a visible exemption. Three hits found and EXCLUDED as measured false positives, not baselined (see the rowSelection allowlist entry). The ratchet refuses to write a HIGHER number (--write-baseline exits 2 without --allow-baseline-growth) and auto-tightens on any passing run whose count is lower, so these two integers can only fall.
